text: I visited this location late on a Sunday night when the Wife and Daughter couldn't wait to get home to eat. We chose Chili's specifically because of their relatively late Sunday night closing time of 11pm. It's only 10pm in Gallatin, e.g. The restaurant was abandoned and only a few drunks remained at the bar. Only bar seating was available, which was fine. Two young ladies took turns waiting on us as they closed down the restaurant. The service was good, considering it had likely already been a long day for staff. We got the white spinach queso which is always great. The girls drank water and I tried the merlot, which was very fruit, and the cabernet, which was much better. The disappointment came with the entree the girls ordered to share. The chicken fingers came in a deep-fried, tempura type batter. It was not bad, per se, it was just odd. It was a little dense, even if it had otherwise seemed appropriate. The fries were only so-so, and the broccoli was raw-not even steamed. The whole thing was kind of off, and if you're thinking, "Well, that's what you should expect on a Sunday night at 10pm", you're right. I did expect that. But I hoped for better. I'm old school and so I think if you're going to claim to remain open until 11, which, let's face it, is not really that late, even for Hendersonville, then you should be in a ready to serve posture. If you don't want to serve that late, then close earlier, and change your hours. But doing things half-assed, just because that's what works most of the time for most people in this country, is a real disappointment. The girls were polite, but didn't hide the fact they wanted us gone. They didn't even address it forthright, as you might expect, by saying, "It's 10pm and no one else is here so we're going to start shutting down the kitchen...", it was just unspoken. I tipped 20% as I always do unless service is horrible, because this is a tough job, but I wasn't thrilled. If it seems that I'm a cranky old man, well, I am 40 and I am generally disappointed by the mediocrity that is common in our culture. I want and hope for best. I hope my experience at this Chili's is unusual.
label: NEG

text: My man and I had so much fun on our spooky date night at Creamy Acres last Friday! We arrived around 8pm and the lines for tickets were super long. Luckily, we had purchased ours in advance so the line for pre-purchased tickets was much shorter. There are two ways to go once you have your tickets: get in line for one of two haunted houses or get in line for the haunted hayride, which actually leads you through two or three other attractions once you are off the hayride. We were encouraged to check out the haunted house first, so we got in line for the one on the left. The line took about 20 minutes or so, but the haunted house was pretty awesome. It took longer to walk through than I expected, or maybe it just felt that way because I was terrified and couldn't wait to get out of it! Next up was the hayride, which was a significantly longer wait time. We probably waited for about 45 minutes to finally board the ride. I was extremely impressed with the ride - for a farm in South Jersey, they really had some amazing special effects and set designs. Totally worth the wait, especially considering the fact that the ride was followed up with a haunted corn maze (which me managed to escape from quickly) and another haunted house, plus a strange but cool haunted rain forest type thing. After all of the screaming, we stopped by the snack bar and enjoyed hot apple cider and a pumpkin donut - just $1 each! VIP tickets allow you to skip the lines but they cost twice as much as regular tickets. My advice would be to go on a weeknight, if possible, to avoid long waits in line. Great night out and would definitely go again.

But who cares really/ My room was clean, bed was comfortable and cleaners provided new towels and soap daily. The neighborhood appeared safe to me. It is close to the "rainbow" district, there are cool/casual eateries around, and as they staff at reception told me "it's possibly the safest area if you are a woman and walk around on your own even at night". I found the turning in my key a bit strange but reception is open 24/7 and I never had problems collecting my key even late at night. Also staff is really nice and welcoming. Nights were overall quiet and had no problems with my sleep. This hotel was just the perfect fit given my schedule. In sum, It's safe and pretty clean. staff and other guests are chilled out and my stay was extremely relaxing. I highly recommend this hotel and will certainly stay at Empress hotel again if I have the chance to go back to NOLA.

It was an endless rotation of Michingan steak (very cheap meat), top sirloin (Picanha - this was the best part), an odd cut of chicken and Calabresa Sausage (which is much better than any other sausage sold in the US). They offered brisket as a replacement for Cupin(A very fatty and tender cut) and a Set of barbecue ribs that I could stop and get one better at any gas station BBQ joint. The ribs were not even close to being Brazilian style and weren't even the same animal. We asked to filet wrapped in bacon, we got something swimming in garlic that we couldn't taste the mean. We asked for chicken hearts, and when it came out, 3 people of my group decided to try them. The chicken hearts were RAW. So much so that, although this is my favorite, i had to spit it out. At the end of the night, we separated the bills. I was charged for 1 meal, + 3 guarana cans (soda) + 2 deserts(to take home for my wife since she does not eat meat) My bill was $66.xx , and for that price, one would expect perfection. Ahhh, and one more thing. The deserts were 3 leches cake, which, according to my wife, Walmart makes it better and a Pudim (Brazilian flan with plum sauce), which was bland, dry and overcooked. (Plum Sauce was good thou) There are better Churrascarias in Orlando, for half the price, if you're willing to drive for 45 minutes, and if you really want good food, i suggest you do. Sorry, i really wanted this place to be good. maybe it was an off night.

text: Condescension without substance. I made a reservation for dinner on Friday night during restaurant week. A busboy/waiter asks if I'm being helped to which I reply, no, I have a reservation for 8. He asks for my name and says someone will be out to help me. The host comes back, ignores me standing there, and immediately walks to and proceeds to seat the couple of two who walked in behind me. I stand, awkwardly, for another couple minutes until I finally realize the area where they are determining which tables are free is around the other side of the bar (a little sign by the door would be nice for those of us who have never been). The host sees me standing by the stack of menus but never bothers to even ask if I'm waiting to be seated. Finally, after having been in the restaurant for almost 5 minutes at this point, I ask if I can be seated as I had a reservation at 8. He tells me he'll check on my table...Oh, they're paying now, it will only be a moment. I notice at this point that there is an empty half booth but figure it is probably reserved for someone else so I stand and wait. 5 more minutes go by and no help. I see another couple walk in and they are immediately seated in another empty table by a different hostess. Furious at this point (It's almost 15 minutes past my reservation time), I go to her and say I have been waiting, I had a reservation at 8 and no one has seated me yet. She tells me she will check on my table and let me know. Mind you, since there is no "waiting area", I have awkwardly been standing in the middle of the bar/restaurant area. She comes back and proceeds to seat me in the half booth that has been empty since I first walked in. Another 10 minutes go by and a waiter finally fills my water and asks me if I would like a drink. I tell him no, I'll wait for the other person in my party (my boyfriend was parking the car at the time). After my boyfriend is seated, we are asked if we want any drinks to start. I ordered a martini, my date ordered a drink and was immediately criticized as though he didn't know what he was asking for. This type of condescension continued the rest of the night. Apparently there is a cheese cart with a waiter who will go around describing the types of cheeses to you? This was never offered to us. Our service was incredibly slow--at one point they brought us out a small salad because we had been waiting 45+ minutes after ordering for our entrees (tortellini and a burger). Overall the worst dining experience I've had so far in Philly. This will definitely be a pass from now on for us.

text: This restaurant is in the space once occupied by Sofia's. It is intimate and cozy, the main dining room seats less than 20 and the bar area maybe 8 more. They have a custom cocktail list like so many great restaurants, and this one is reminiscent of the Franklin Mortgage and Investment Co., with its emphasis on brown liquids in all sorts of interesting combinations. The service was excellent, and personalized, she knew what to do and say for each customer. On to the food which was very protein-heavy, which I like. Then again, I like everything. I started with the beef tartare. The texture was very unctuous, soft and almost pudding-like. It felt wonderful on the mouth. Hints of mustard, citrus, perfectly seasoned but not overpowered. Some chefs feel the need to disguise the beef, not here. The accompanying bread slices were toasted with just a hint of cheese, again quite subtle, and there was a schmeer of a parsley-like very green puree that you could dip into as you wished. Very good! Just one note, there was too much bread so I didn't finish it. The second course was a special veal cheeks with sweetbreads. The meats were cooked perfectly, and the sauce, while quite rich and strong, was beautiful. The cheeks were even more tender than a falling-apart short rib. The main course was rabbit "pot-au-feu", I put that in parentheses because every pot-au-feu I have had has been much simpler and not very interesting. This dish was a complex mix of flavors, colors and textures, and included carrots and potatoes and a crostini with liver on it that complimented each bite fantastically. The sauce again was rich and soft. Coaxed to have dessert, I noted only three on the menu, all simple. I had the creme brûlée and it was what I consider perfect, which is to say that the texture was just slightly thinner than pudding. Creme brûlée should not be custardy or eggy, I think. Real vanilla beans of course, great caramelized crust. Bibou is the top feminine French bistro in Philly with its more delicate treatments of food, and I think Townsend must be the top masculine one. A bold menu that screams protein. Arrhh! Yum.
label: POS

text: The High Level Bridge is the iconic bridge of Edmonton. It was built by the CPR and opened in 1913 joining the Cities of Edmonton and Strathcona. From its onset the bridge was designed to accommodate railcars, streetcars, pedestrians and automobiles. The Edmonton Radial Railway operates the Streetcar during the summer months and it is a cheap ride to take to get from Old Strathcona to Downtown, with an amazing view as you cross the river. Often the bridge is depicted in artwork of the City because it is that iconic bridge of our City. text: This was our 3rd and last time here. First of all, we moved from Hawaii to Reno recently, so we've eaten at various L&Ls arcross Hawaii. When in Hawaii, you can pretty much expect that each franchised location will cook and prepare in similar fashion, which means food tastes almost identical no matter which location you chose. I understand that with different regions, ingredient quality and supply will vary, so taste may be slightly affected. I can accept that. The previous 2 times here, I was not impressed. But since we really wanted to love the L&L in the area we now call home, Reno, we kept saying to give it another try. It was nice thinking we could still have a little comfort food that we are accustomed to from "back home", in Hawaii. So here's how our final visit went... We walked in to a pretty empty restaurant. There we're maybe 2 groups already sitting and eating their food. We we're greeted by a friendly (local) girl at the counter. Our group of 4 stand and stare at the menu for a few minutes. In those few minutes, we witness a very unsettling incident...a customer brings his food to the counter to tell the girl that he found a metal shard in his food (they figured it to be the metal from a brillo-like scrubber). The cashier doesn't hesitate at all, she quickly handles the situation. Stating she will have the cook prepare a new fresh plate. She sends the order back to the cook, who begins stating he can't cook a new meal without an order reciept(?). Immediately another female comes out from the back area, asking the cashier if there is a way to print a new order receipt. This goes back and forth as discussion between the two girls for a minute. Finally, its resolved, however, when the female returns to the back area, the cook angrily speaks to her, in a tone loud enough for us customers in the front to overhear. It made me think about leaving, but the rest of my party wanted to stay and eat. So, we proceed to order our food. Okay, no biggie, we sit down and patiently wait for our food. While waiting, we see the female employee who the cooked just got finishing yelling at, walking outside...I felt so bad for her, in my opinion, she did nothing wrong, except attempt to correct an order for a customer. She was a champ! She maintained her composure, cooled off, and then went back to helping customers. Now here's the kicker!! Our food finally arrives, we eagerly open our plate lunches, anticipating some ono food. Bah humbug! My pork tocino, can't tell if it's raw or cooked. My plate, which doesn't come with mac salad, has pieces of mac salad here and there. My rice, some of it was so hard and formed little ball-like chunks. My sister's plate, she found a single hair mixed into her tossed green salad. OK, she tries to look past it and enjoy her food. My nephew, he has pork pieces placed underneath his CHICKEN katsu?! Say what?! Chicken katsu doesn't include any pork! My hubby, although his BBQ mixed plate isn't exact of Hawaii's own plate, he still tries to enjoy it. Okay, that's just way too much! I keep moving my pieces of pork around on my plate asking if it is cooked. My awesome hubby gets up to call one of the girls over, he quietly, without making a scene, begins to tell her of the many issues with our orders. we figured, if this was an isolated incident, no need for others to overhear and think twice about their food. Again, this girl is a champ! No hesitation, she apologizes and offers a refund. Okay, I'll accept that. We tell her we witnessed the confrontation earlier with the cook and that we we're sorry for her to have to deal with that. We also let her know L&L in Hawaii was of much higher quality than this. And unfortunately, we will most likely never return to this L&L ever again. This is not about bashing L&L or it's employees. While the cook might need some replacing, those girls are friendly and know good customer service. Its very unfortunate that as a customer, we are subjected to the poor leadership of a company. It's the few bad apples that can bring down the entire reputation of a business. I DO hope the owners of this L&L location are awakened to the fact that they need better leadership for their employees. And, if you're looking for good ono plate lunches, sadly, there's none to be found here.

text: Came here for a celebratory homecoming dinner after my main squeeze had been overseas for two months, and it was a great choice! When you pull in you will be required to valet your car. Notice all the Maseratis, Porsches, BMWs, and Mercedes' flanking the entrance to the restaurant. If you drive a crappy VW like me, it will be hidden way in the back so as not to scar the delicate eyeballs of Mainline 1%ers. The valet is gratis, though, so that's a plus! They were also very fast when retrieving my car at the end of the evening. Noise level was deafening upon entry for an 8pm reservation, but had simmered down a bit by the end of our meal. Dress code was not as formal as the vehicular lineup and valet theatrics would indicate. It was as though everyone was on the same mailing list that informs wealthy white people of what to wear and when, which must also be the medium by which all Mainline housewives know just the right level of upscale athleisure and gold accessories that is appropriate for an afternoon grocery run. Lots of very tan people in the 40s-early 60s age range. The few people I saw closer to our age were with groups that appeared to include their parents. OK, you're reading this for the food, not my snarky classist commentary. We decided to start by sharing a seafood bento and crispy octopus salad. The presentation of the octopus was lovely - it arrived in a covered dish and when the lid was removed with a flourish, bonito flakes danced a delicate, wavy jig on top of the crispy octopus. This dish was excellent and got F's vote for best dish of the night. The seafood bento was also very good - each component included thoughtful accompaniments that were much more than a typical afterthought garnish. Only the shrimp spring roll stood out as rather pedestrian, though not bad by any means, while everything else was spectacular. The tuna tartare in the bento was my favourite item of the night. We moved on to share two specialty sushi rolls, which are quite large. The seared tuna was very good, but didn't stand out as anything really special or unusual to justify the price tag. If it had incorporated a yuzu vinaigrette drizzle or something else to brighten it up I think I would have been more wowed. The King Kong roll was better in theory than in practice. The overall impression was a bit dry, and I'm personally not huge on shishito leaf so that's just my own taste. The end pieces were so huge there was no way to eat them whole, so I pulled out the meats to eat on their own. I found that the beef was incredibly good and it seemed sort of a crime to hide it in a roll like that. A bit gimmicky, and not terribly successful. Finally we each concluded with our own dessert, always the highlight of the meal for F. He got the chocolate torte and I went with the deconstructed s'more. His torte was very good, rich and beautifully presented but not unique or particularly interesting. My s'more suffered the same fate nearly every Top Chef contestant meets in the "deconstruct a dish" challenge. Each component was good on its own, but did not come together in a single bite to evoke the flavour of a s'more. It was also a little confused, with peanut butter and banana being brought to the party. The chocolate peanut butter brulee was interesting but lacked the smooth creaminess of a traditional creme brulee; the banana marshmallows didn't taste much like banana but the torched exteriors were very satisfying; the banana ice cream could have been creamier (it was icy, more like a sorbet) and the graham cracker cake's texture did not play well with the other components, while tasty on its own. To accompany this feast I got a thyme and cucumber gin cocktail that was truly excellent, well balanced with good flavour. In fact, it was so good I decided to get two even though I was planning to only have one, but was then disappointed when my second drink arrived tasting significantly different from the first - sweeter, and less balanced. It was still fine and I drank it, but it speaks to an inconsistent regime behind the bar. The bill was actually not that shocking, especially by Center City standards. Total before tax and tip was about $122, which I found fairly reasonable. Service was good and overall we really enjoyed our experience. We plan to come back in the future for drinks and a full table of appetizers - those were the real stars of the menu and could easily make a meal. We found what we had ordered to be the perfect amount of food, we left full but not stuffed.

text: I am not one who usually complains or gives reviews but I believe that this experience warranted one. We have lived in New Orleans for 2 years and have been lucky enough to try many of the wonderful restaurants this city has to offer. This particular dinner was meant to be a celebration of graduating medical school. We originally wanted to go to Peche but they were unable to accommodate us as we were a rather large party (14). They recommended we try their sister restaurant Herbsaint. The biggest faux pas of the evening, and what in my opinion is unforgivable, was that 2/4 of the black drum entrees were heinously undercooked. This is not a fish where a little raw in the middle is ok. The fish was not served with any vegetables or accoutrement. It was literally just a bland, baked, piece of drum with a side of pureed (mashed) potatoes that were cold. The rest of the entrees were alright but nothing to write home about. The only thing that was decent was the teres minor and french fries, so if you do make the mistake of wandering into this god forsaken establishment, order that. The service was average at best with the waiter acting somewhere between ambivalent and annoyed. The meals were pricey and unimaginative. In the ever changing restaurant ecosystem that is New Orleans I hope that natural selection takes it's course and that Herbsaint is rapidly made extinct.

text: Received some excellent service at this Earl's location last night while doing some last minute Christmas shopping with the masses at WEM. After being greeted by the trio of hostesses waiting outside, we sat ourselves at a table in the lounger and was greeting promptly by our server. She asked us for our drink orders. I only wanted water with lemon and my fiance ordered an iced tea. One of the managers promptly brought over our drinks and even remembered the lemon I requested. I ordered the bacon and cheddar burger with fries, while my fiance ordered a steak, rare, with a side of grilled prawns. The food came out in a decent time. Unfortunately, my fiance's steak was overcooked so he told our server who quickly took it back to be remedied. But before leaving, she asked him he wanted something else to nibble on while he waited, which he declined as he could have some of my meal. No sooner had she left, that the same manager who brought us our drink order, came by the table to apologize and also reaffirm that the kitchen was working on a new order. Between the two of us, we finished my burger and fries before his meal reappeared. I should mention my burger was pretty good, full of flavor, if not a touch too salty. The fries on the other hand, were lukewarm at best. When his order arrived (via the manager), she now asked me if I wanted something else to eat while waiting, and she offered up their seasonal dessert special, which was a warm gingerbread cake with caramelized apples and vanilla ice cream. How could I pass that up?! So I happily agreed and sure enough, they brought out a complimentary dessert for me. How very nice! And it was so yummy! Moist and full of flavour, it totally invoked Christmas in my tastebuds! I wish I could've finished it all but alas I ended up having to take most of it home as a delicious leftover. So my fiance's new steak was prepared to his liking... the prawns he ordered on the side were a whopping 12! The steak came with roasted yams and beets (both delicious!) plus mashed potatoes (which I also enjoyed!). In the meantime, throughout the dinner service, our server brought over a new refilled iced tea for my fiance several times without asking, which I thought was a nice touch -anticipating needs! Needless to say, we both had a great meal with excellent attention to service and we made a point of not only tipping to reflect that but also made sure we told our server we were impressed by her service. Nicely done Earls! We will be back...

text: I never thought I'd be writing a review of a funeral home, but I want people to know about my experience. My parents were kind and smart enough to make advance arrangements with Memorial Park many years ago. Even in that situation, planning for a funeral is a difficult and emotional task. The folks at Memorial Park understand this and were a total blessing to us. When my mother passed away, I called around 5:30 on a Friday, thinking no one would be there and that I'd have to try again on Monday. I left a message and, within a few minutes, Eric returned my call. He was kind, professional and compassionate. He took some information about my mom and let me know that her body was in their care. They use that word a lot - care - and it's appropriate, because I and my family received the best of care from them from start to finish. We provided preliminary information to Eric and made an appointment for Saturday to come in, sign papers, and make decisions and arrangements When you walk into the office at Memorial Park, you will always be greeted by someone who is very professional and courteous. They will offer you water, snacks and a comfortable seat before showing you to a consultation room. Melanie and Kristen were our primary points of contact, but over the course of weeks, I worked with many people, and they were all absolutely fantastic. Melanie was our funeral director, so she helped us take care of arrangements for mom's cremation (paperwork, etc), getting death certificates, and helping us arrange the memorial service. She was responsive (even returning emails on her days off) and delightful to work with. My mom wasn't affiliated with a church, so we used the facilities at Memorial Park for her service and a reception. The facilities are beautiful. When I arrived on the day of mom's service (we brought our own food in for the reception, but you can have caterers deliver food and drink as well), the chapel was already set up. Flowers had been placed, a guestbook and prayer cards were there. Georgia Devero set up/break down the reception room, and she was a blessing, attending to every detail. Rachel Troutt was the funeral director who was on duty when we had mom's service, and she was amazing as well. Attentive to every need, on top of every minor detail. Two older gentlemen - Roger and Frank - were also there to assist and did a fantastic job attending to anything and everything we needed plus acting basically as ushers for the service. The facility has audio/visual capabilities, and we developed a DVD with a slide show of pictures coordinated with music. Rachel did a great job executing on that portion of the service, queueing up everything perfectly. We had also set up photos and albums of mom in the back of the chapel for people to look at as they came in and left. While we were receiving attendees in the reception room, Roger and Frank took everything down and packed it carefully away for us in bags to help make it easier for us to take everything home when we left. They even helped move the flowers from the service over to my parents' niche after the service, carrying a big wreath of flowers on a brutally hot August day. When my mother's remains were ready, we scheduled an internment service to place them in the niche my parents bought, where my dad's ashes were already laid to rest. Again, Kristin and Rachel were on-hand to help. It was raining cats and dogs, and when we got there, they had everything set up in a place indoors where we could say a few words and not get wet. They even had a cooler of bottled water for us. After the ceremony, we needed to take the ashes over to the niche, and it was still storming outside. Rather than have us all get wet, Rachel and Kristen walked back to the funeral home and brought back umbrellas for everyone so we could walk to the niche without getting wet. I could go on and on about these folks. Every single person we came in contact with was absolutely professional, helpful and compassionate. I can't imagine that their jobs are easy but they do a great job. They are also very tightly integrated. Each person has a different function and sometimes they cover for each other, but they never once dropped the ball. I must also mention that funeral homes sometimes have a reputation for trying to sell you things you don't need/want and trying to take advantage of you during an emotionally vulnerable time. At no time did that happen with Memorial Park. While we had plans in advance, they still could have upsold us on things but never did. They laid out options, let us make choices and answered questions helpfully and honestly, even giving us tips to save on the few costs not covered by my parents' plans. They made the worst experience of my life bearable, helped me when I needed it, and gave me things I didn't know I needed to make it easier. I consider them a true blessing. Thank you, Memorial Park and bless you all!

text: In the interest of disclosure, this restaurant probably deserves 4.5 stars because I've had some pretty mediocre service before. However, I went last night and the service was on point so I bumped it up to five. I went because someone told me they have the best fish and chips in Tucson. It's funny because I've never actually tried the fish and chips, but I haven't gone wrong yet! It's a large, single room pub. Very loud, so you won't want to come if you're looking for a romantic outing. As others have mentioned, lots of military memorabilia everywhere. I like it and I'm happy to support the business of a local Tucson veteran as my husband is also a veteran. I'm impressed at the appeal this place has to a large variety of demographics. I came here one night and felt very out of place because it was loaded with college students (my college days are behind me), but come another night and you'll see mostly folks in their 40s, or groups of older ladies, or groups of veterans, or mid 20s people like me looking for some good food. I like that because it feels very inclusive. Excellent atmosphere to have at a pub and I wonder how they do it - I bet a lot of people would pay the owners for their secrets on how to appeal to everybody like that. I could absolutely see myself becoming a regular here. Now, onto the food, the most important part! The first time I came here I had the Chesapeake Bay burger because I am an Old Bay freak. Big, stuffed with goodies, and excellent flavor. However, they have lighter dishes that will actually appeal to you rather than forcing you to feel like, "Crap, I'm on a diet, I guess I'll have this nasty wilted salad." I came here the other night and wanted to try their famous clam chowder. I had a soup and sandwich combo with the chicken salad sandwich. Now, I still think that my grandma's chowder is better, but I won't say that I didn't enjoy that chowder immensely. At request they top it with a generous bit of bacon and green onions. Yum! The sandwich impressed me a lot as well because you don't see chicken salad everywhere, but it's one of my favorites. It comes on toasted bread with the perfect amount of chicken salad. And it's not an overly sweet salad either. You know I liked it because I came back the next night and had the exact same thing. Ok, so, the service. Last night it was out of the park. Jason noticed me at the door looking for a table and used his immense height to locate one for me in the nearly-full house. He was very pleasant and even checked on me later to see how I was doing. Janelle was my server and she was amazing. I order coffee when I come here rather than a beer because as much as I love beer, I work graveyards and need to wake up before my shift. This usually means that they have to brew a new pot because I don't know who else comes there for coffee at 9pm on a Friday night except me. However, she did so without complaint. She was always prompt and had a smile on her face the whole time. She knew what the soup of the day was without having to go check (other servers at this place sometimes don't...) and I just adored her. Never once felt ignored - and I was a one top taking up a table on a busy night. Thank you, Janelle! As for other service I've had, it would echo what countless other reviewers have mentioned. Young, pretty college girls who have a little trouble paying attention to their tables. Like I said, they often don't know the specials, and you might have to chase them across the restaurant for the check, where you'll probably find them sitting at the bar, chatting with their friends. I don't get worked up about it because I know what restaurant work is like, it can be a grind, and they will go get my check if asked. It is sort of irksome that I have to go find them, though. It's also a little annoying that this is my usual experience with the service here, rather than Janelle the rockstar. A note to the restaurant: if half your yelp reviews echo this experience with the service (which they do), maybe work on a little server training. It's ok to socialize, restaurants are social places, but you also need to do your job while on the clock. Like I said, though, I'm still giving this place five stars because I love it. Come here and you won't be disappointed.

text: For a special occasion, be sure to get a booth For this visit my wife made reservations for us on open table.com for our 12th wedding anniversary. When we arrived we were greeted by the hostess who took our last name, fiddled around for what seemed like two or three minutes, and then asked us to follow her to our table. We were situated in what was basically the middle of the room on a four top. Before we sat down, my wife and I actually teetered on whether or not we should request a booth or not, but we ultimately remained seated at this table thinking that the restaurant must have been full which is why we ended up with this table. Later we would discover that we were completely incorrect on that assumption and that we could have been given a much more romantic booth. We would also later learn that this restaurant actually has about a dozen secluded booths which we discovered on our way out, poking our heads into different rooms as we made our way to the door. Honestly, I found that to be truly inexcusable as we purposely made the restaurant aware that we were there for our anniversary several times over. We started the evening with the pear and brie cheese fondue and a bottle of the Mirassou Pinot Noir for $30. The wine is a fairly decent bottle which would normally set you back $10 in the store. It has strawberry undertones and we found it to be quite delightful for our meal. The fondue was served with a small bowl of vegetables including mostly cauliflower, followed by celery, and carrots. In another bowl we found Granny Smith apples and lastly a large bowl of sliced bread, which was a mixture of French and a couple of pieces of wheat/French bread. I would suggest asking for just bread during this phase of your meal as the other items do not allow you to actually experience the wonderful blend of cheeses and pears. In fact, I'd venture to say that the vegetables will actually leave you scratching your head as to why they are served in the first place. We decided not to get any salads, and instead move directly to entrées. It is suggested that you get two or three of the entrée choices to make up each individuals meal. While I found this to be spot on in terms of portion size, I do have a few suggestions. My wife and I each ordered filet mignon, and I ordered the lobster tail and my wife ordered the shrimp as our second entrées. I am going to guess that the portion sizes for each plate are around 4 ounces. We both found the fillets to be perfect cuts of meat. The lobster tail was cut into four pieces and was very strangely sprinkled with some sort of red granular spice that neither of us could identify. This seemed to detract from the overall taste of the lobster so much so that for my second piece I actually dumped it in my water glass and swirled it around until most of that "red seasoning" was absent. Then and only then did the lobster actually taste like lobster. Overall for the $9.50 you pay for the lobster tail I'd recommend skipping it. Same was true unfortunately for the shrimp as well. You only get three shrimp for the price, making them difficult to share and they are large shrimp not jumbo, which makes the value poor. It would probably be better to either double up on the filet which was an excellent choice or perhaps grab another protein. We also decided to try the macaroni and cheese and grilled vegetables as a couple of additional sides. The description of the macaroni and cheese sounded delightful and we asked about it with our server he said it was truly incredible. I have a couple of very important suggestion I have regarding side items. First, skip the vegetables as they were just "okay" as a mixture of zucchini, green peppers and string beans, mostly. Next, I would advise that if you do get a side item such as the macaroni and cheese which was incredibly delightful it would be best for you to eat that first as the rest of your meal will wait. We decided to nibble on this along the way and unfortunately about halfway through our entrées we discovered that it got cold a little too quickly and didn't taste as nearly as good at room temperature as it did when it was hot. For dessert we decided on the "Dark and Dulce" and a couple of glasses of Grand Marnier. The dessert was described as "a classic flavor combination featuring our dark chocolate and sweet, thick dulce de leche accented with coarse ground sea salt". It was served with an assortment of side items on one, plate, even though you pay per person. Items included some bananas, strawberries, poundcake, rice crispy treats, blonde and chocolate brownies and dusted marshmallows. Other than the fruit, everything we tried seemed off. I'd swear that the rice crispy treats were actually stale. We ended up asking for additional strawberries and bananas and giving back the entire plate. We were brought out a couple of bowls of strawberries and bananas both of which were quite fresh and delicious. Overall this dessert tasted wonderful

text: I've been to Yoi Tomo half a dozen times and have always had a good experience, but our visit tonight was horrible. I arrived at 5:30 and ordered a few things while waiting for my wife and kids to finish their movie across the street. For the first 15 minutes, things were fine, but as it got close to 6:00 pm, things started falling apart. I would estimate that by 6:15 the place was full, with about 50 diners. There were only two sushi chefs and two waitresses, so getting anything - even a glass of water - was a challenge. The kids meal I ordered for my daughter took 45 minutes to come out, so I shared some of the AYCE sushi I had ordered with her. The problem was that it would take a long time for a waitress to get over to us, and once we ordered something it would take 20+ minutes for it to come out - for an all-you-can-eat place, that's a big problem: you order a little bit, eat it, and then sit around doing nothing for close to half an hour while you wait for the next sushi roll you ordered to be made. After watching our waitress rush by our table four times without stopping to clear plates or see if we needed anything, I went to the manager/owner, who's also a sushi chef and asked if I could just order at the sushi counter. The owner did what he could to get the food out, but the simple problem was that they were overwhelmed. But after waiting another 20-some minutes to get a bowl of miso soup for my hungry kids, I told him that I would pay what he thought was fair and was leaving to buy dinner somewhere else. I ended up paying $65 for an all-you-can-eat that was about 25% of what I wanted to eat and three times longer than we wanted to hang around waiting for food. I can be somewhat sympathetic about restaurants being very busy, but if you can't serve your customers properly you should probably stop seating people, hire some more staff, or go into a different line of business. I won't be going back to Yoi Tomo. There are too many dining options in the downtown area to have to sit around for hours waiting for raw fish on rice to be plated and served. Next time I'm in the mood for sushi, I'll try Sushi Ya or another place.

text: I found South Philly Psychic via Yelp and the very helpful review of Vinny L. and with the urging a friend. I've been to a couple psychics before, one at a psychic fair in a nursing home as a high-schooler, where I was told that that summer I would have two boyfriends who would fight over me - not fulfilled! And another in Old City who told me and my two friends that none of the men we were dating were the right ones for us, which given our ages could have been a lucky guess. She also told me that I should return to school to work on my writing because it would prove lucrative. Shout out to that psychic, I'm in debt! I've always felt a little uncomfortable around psychics, kind of like when I go to get my haircut and I want extra attention and advice and they just give me long layers and ask me where I go to school. It's never enough and I always feel like I'm overpaying. I climbed the narrow, steep shag carpeted stairs of South Street Psychic avoiding the piles of catalogs and coupon books sliding down around my feet. A face appeared at the door - almost as if she knew I was coming! "Are you hear for a reading, my dear?" said the woman at the door. We made an appointment for an hour later, and hit the bar in the meantime. Note to future customers: Roxanne has a lot going on, and her business might be a front for something else, so best to book ahead. You think you're the only person in the city who wants to know whether they're going to die alone? When we returned, my friend made me do my reading first. I didn't have enough money for the tarot reading but was stupid enough to get the combination aura and palm reading. Although the space is presented as a storefront, Roxanne performs her services in what appears to be her house, at her kitchen table. I noticed a bag of Friskies Indoor Delights - also my brand! So a point for Roxanne on that front. Roxanne seemed stressed and preoccupied while giving me my reading - after she shut down her game of Candy Crush she checked her text messages at least twice and received a call once. Scrolling through her Twitter feed, she noted that my aura was purple with a little bit of stress clouds hanging around, and that I seemed like a good person and I had good energy - which is the exact thing I'd wanted her to say. She barked at me to put my hands on the table, and after getting up to open the door for the Verizon guy, who then took his place feet away from us in the living room, she said I was going to have more than three children - possibly around four. The specificity of the number was what really got me. She also told me that an old flame would enter my life again soon, but that it wouldn't be good. Someone I regrettably hooked up with three years ago LITERALLY viewed my LinkedIn profile this week, so I'm going to give Roxanne another point for that. My friend's tarot card reading was more extensive. Roxanne told her she was going to have a baby within the next year! Terrifying. As the Verizon guy and I stood in the living room - and I need to say that a point against the space is its total lack of ambience: the ESP Tarot light-up sign piled high with athletic caps and a 12 bottle pack of Mountain Dew, for example - he whispered to me, "If she was really psychic she would know what was wrong with her internet."

I spend an extra couple of minutes looking for Enterprise space 6 when my car was in Alamo space 6. No biggie, it's a small airport, with a small rental lot. There's a couple of gas stations right by the airport, so don't buy the full tank ahead of time, just arrive in the vicinity a little early to fill up before returning. Return is as easy as check out, it's right outside the terminal so much more convenient than at larger airports, and the prices are very good too. I looked here on Yelp for the highest rated Italian restaurants, and came up with a few options. After looking at reviews, menus, and location, I was most interested in Gio's. I read that the location was tucked away in a strip mall and a little hard to find, so the tip to look for Gold's Gym was helpful. I just took I-275 to Busch Gardens, turned right on Florida, then right on Waters, and it is on the right before Dale Mabry. The outside of Gio's has an awning and a little bit of outside seating. Once entering, we were greeted, and promptly led to a table. It was lunchtime, and there was only one other table occupied. The dining room is fairly small, but makes good use of the space. There are wine bottles lining the wall, and a piano at the front, which is played on the weekends. The atmosphere felt a little classy actually, with dimmer lighting, a flower on each table, and nice tablecloths. As I always do before going to a restaurant, I checked out the menu online to see what I would order. I had narrowed my choices to two pasta dishes, the Linguini Di Mare (Seafood linguini. Linguini with shrimp, calamari, clams, mussels and scallops in white or red tomato marinara sauce) and the Linguini Alla Vongole (Linguini with clams. Linguini with fresh clams in a red or white wine sauce). However, when I heard one of their specials was lobster ravioli, I promptly changed my mind. While waiting for our entrees we were brought bread and house salads, which come with lunch entrees. The bread was soft thankfully, because I hate getting bread where the crust might break my tooth. The house salad was very good, containing mixed greens, carrots, and their homemade dressing. Additonally, we ordered the Bruschetta Al Pomodoro appetizer (Thinly sliced fresh baguette brushed with olive oils and garlic and topped with fresh chopped tomato and basil). I really liked my lobster ravioli, which was done in their princess sauce, and contained a nice amount of filling. There were five ravioli, which was a good portion for me. My boyfriend ordered the Vitello Millanese (Veal dish. Pounded veal lightly breaded and topped with homemade bruschetta), and came with a side of bowtie pasta. The lunch prices are pretty reasonable, I think our entrees were about $13-$15. We took a peak at the dinner menu, and those items are quite pricey for us (in the $20s). The service was very good, and we had several different people remove finished plates and refill drinks. We will definitely go back for lunch.

text: I've never experienced anything as unbelievable as to what happened at this hotel. I travel regularly as the owner of two companies and this was my first time staying at an Omni Hotel. After a long week of travel, my partner met me to see the gateway arch and explore the city museum, two local attractions. When we got back to our room that night, we were in shock. Our room, 208, was directly above the bar that had music louder than a dance club. This was at 11:30 at night. We decided to relax thinking they certainly could not go past midnight. They did. I called the front desk and they did not answer, probably because they knew why I was calling. I called again and the staff member picked up...you could hear the music clear as day though the handset. I asked her when the music would be shut down as we needed to sleep (It was now 12:05 AM), she told us they were going until 1:00. I asked if there was anything they could do as we were very tired, like move us to a different room, and she said no...but she would leave a note for the manager. We continued to listen to music that was conversation level in our room with lyrics that were derogatory to African Americans and the LGBT community and a song about something called truffle butter that comes from lady parts. We were both in shock that the hotel would allow such explicit music to be played in an open lobby area at 12:30 at night - especially when it could be heard clearly on the 2nd floor. It left us wide awake wondering what they meant by things like truffle butter - quite disturbing as we are a gay couple. Finally at 12:50 they shut down the music, and our room became peaceful - we had no other complaints about the room besides the fact that we could not sleep until 1:00 AM. We were taken aback when in the morning they slipped the hotel bill under our door without even an acknowledgement of what had happened overnight. Surely I thought to myself that the manager at the front desk was ready to rectify the situation. When I went to check out he said the total and told us to have a good day. I told him that we had a terrible night in the room (208) and told him a note was left for the manager to discuss with us in the morning. He told us he was the manager and wasn't aware. We explained what happened and he told us they would take off our parking for the night. That seemed like a pittance given that from 10 PM on most hotels will enforce a noise ordnance and throw guests out that do not comply. Our only option was to lay awake in our bed and listen to the disgusting lyrics in our room, some of which were highly offensive to a gay couple. I told him I would not have paid anything for the room or stayed at the hotel had I known this would have been our experience and he said, "I'm sorry for the inconvenience." We left infuriated at the situation and how poor customer service is at the Omni Majestic Hotel and that they felt free parking justifies keeping guests up until 1:00 AM without any prior notice. Certainly we will never be staying in this hotel again, and it brings into question the Omni brand being that this was our first experience.

So please allow me to set you straight. Pepperfire, like Hattie B's, may achieve high marks from tourists who haven't eaten enough hot chicken to make a fair comparison, but both of these restaurants are huge disappointments when you've had the "real thing." The chicken I had at Pepperfire was much like Hattie B's, crispy outside but dry and flavorless inside. And mediocre french fries to boot. Good enough for a Music City visitor ignorant of the rights and wrongs of this gastronomic phenomenon, but not good enough for my discerning palate! If you are a tourist looking for the real deal, PLEASE listen to an expert. If I had one last meal, it would be the absolutely perfect breast quarter (with a side of hot catfish) from Big Shake's in downtown Franklin!!!
